steps.title: Gather Materials and Reagents
steps.instruction: Collect all listed consumables, glassware, tubing, valves, Arduino boards, mp6‑OEM controllers, logic level converters, Pi Cobbler breakout board, double‑sided adhesive tape, razor blades, scalpel handles, surgical tools, filter papers, and chemical reagents (CaCl₂, MgCl₂, MgSO₄, KCl, NaCl, NaH₂PO₄, NaHCO₃, D‑glucose, isoflurane solution, ODNs, 100 % O₂, 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂).

steps.title: Assemble Breadboard Power Rails
steps.instruction: Use a breadboard with three 63‑row terminal strips (e.g., Digilent 340‑002‑1 or Wisher WBU‑206). Remove the rightmost power distribution bus and its adjacent terminal strip. Attach two Arduino Uno boards staggered on the board using screws or Velcro pads. Connect a 5 V DC power supply to the horizontal distribution bus (red “+”, black “–”). Add a SPST toggle master switch to control power to the circuit.

steps.title: Wire Horizontal and Vertical Buses
steps.instruction: Connect the power and ground of all vertical distribution buses to the 5 V and ground rails of the horizontal bus, respectively.

steps.title: Install Potentiometers
steps.instruction: Mount two 10 kΩ potentiometers on the middle (now rightmost) terminal strip. Connect each potentiometer to 5 V and ground. Ensure the wiper‑adjusting screws face away from each other to allow clearance for a mini‑screwdriver.

steps.title: Set Potentiometer Voltages
steps.instruction: Using a mini‑screwdriver, adjust the top potentiometer to give 1.3 V across its wiper and the bottom potentiometer to give 1.8 V across its wiper. Disconnect the power supply before proceeding to the next steps.

steps.title: Mount Logic Level Converters
steps.instruction: Install two 8‑channel logic level converters on the same terminal strip as the potentiometers. Connect VCCB of each converter to 5 V and GND to ground. Connect VCCA and OE of the top converter to 1.3 V and of the bottom converter to 1.8 V using gray jumper wires.

steps.title: Attach Pi Cobbler Breakout
steps.instruction: Place the 26‑pin assembled Pi Cobbler breakout board on the breadboard using shield‑stacking headers to elevate it, providing clearance for the third and fourth mp6‑OEM controllers that will be attached later.

steps.title: Connect mp6‑OEM Controllers
steps.instruction: Insert six mp6‑OEM controllers into the leftmost terminal strip. For the bottom two controllers (inflow lines), connect Pin 2 (cyan) to the bottom Arduino Uno (see Step 22). For the top four controllers (suction), short Pins 2 and 3 (no Arduino input) and leave Pins 5 and 10 unused. Short Pins 11 and 12 on all six controllers with U‑shaped jumper loops. Short Pins 2 and 3 on the top four controllers with five‑pointed asterisks. Connect ground (black) to Pin 1 (white spot) and 5 V (red) to Pin 14 on all six controllers.

steps.title: Wire 1.3 V to Pin 4
steps.instruction: From pins A1‑A6 of the top logic level converter, run yellow 1.3 V wires to Pin 4 of all six mp6‑OEM controllers.

steps.title: Wire 1.8 V to Pin 13
steps.instruction: From pins A1‑A6 of the bottom logic level converter, run orange 1.8 V wires to Pin 13 of all six mp6‑OEM controllers.

steps.title: Connect Pi Cobbler Pin 6
steps.instruction: Link Pin 6 (brown) on the Pi Cobbler to the left‑side pins 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 of the breakout board.

steps.title: Connect Pi Cobbler Pin 7
steps.instruction: Link Pin 7 (green) on the Pi Cobbler to the left‑side pins 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 of the breakout board.

steps.title: Connect Pi Cobbler Pin 8
steps.instruction: Link Pin 8 (blue) on the Pi Cobbler to the right‑side pins 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 of the breakout board.

steps.title: Connect Pi Cobbler Pin 9
steps.instruction: Link Pin 9 (purple) on the Pi Cobbler to the left‑side pins 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 of the breakout board.

steps.title: Wire Top Logic Converter to Top Arduino
steps.instruction: Connect inputs B1‑B6 of the top logic level converter to Digital Pins 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 of the top Arduino Uno (white cables).

steps.title: Wire Bottom Logic Converter to Top Arduino
steps.instruction: Connect inputs B1‑B6 of the bottom logic level converter to Digital Pins 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 of the top Arduino Uno (magenta cables).

steps.title: Connect Bottom Arduino PWM Outputs
steps.instruction: Run PWM0 (output 9) and PWM1 (output 10) of the bottom Arduino Uno to Pin 2 (cyan) of the two inflow mp6‑OEM controllers.

steps.title: Link ADC to Top Arduino
steps.instruction: Connect one digital output of the NI ADC board to TX 1 and GND of the top Arduino Uno (see Figure 2A). This line will trigger the perfusion program via the winLTP software.

steps.title: Ground Bottom Arduino
steps.instruction: Connect GND of the bottom Arduino to the central ground of the electrophysiology rig (the top Arduino is grounded via the ADC ground, see Step 24).

steps.title: Upload Arduino Programs
steps.instruction: Copy the program shown in Figure 18 to the bottom Arduino (Microcontroller 2) and the program shown in Figure 19 to the top Arduino (Microcontroller 1). Connect both Arduinos to a computer via USB.

steps.title: Assemble mp6‑OEM Cable Harness
steps.instruction: Prepare six 4‑wire 32 AWG multi‑conductor cables (e.g., MC001 Alpha Wire). For each mp6‑OEM, attach a male gold‑plated pin to each of its four Molex connector pins, then insert the cable into the 26‑pin ribbon breakout board. Use the color scheme (clockwise from top‑left socket: brown, purple, blue, green) for all six connectors; only 24 of the 26 sockets are used.

steps.title: Build Two‑Pump Sandwiches
steps.instruction: Cut three custom plexiglass spacers as in Figures 15A‑B. Glue the marked side of mp6‑1 to a spacer with double‑sided tape, add a cork pad to the unmarked side (order: plexiglass/mp6‑1/cork). For mp6‑2, glue a cork pad to the marked side and a spacer to the unmarked side (order: cork/mp6‑2/plexiglass).

steps.title: Construct Four‑Pump Array
steps.instruction: Stack the two sandwich assemblies with a third (unglued) plexiglass spacer between them, yielding: plexiglass/mp6‑1/cork/plexiglass/cork/mp6‑2/plexiglass. Secure with double‑sided tape, a clamp, or long screws that pass through drilled holes in only one spacer (tap threads in that spacer).

steps.title: Make Mini‑Faraday Cages
steps.instruction: Form copper‑wire mesh cages around each pump assembly (Figure 15F) and ground them to the main air‑table ground to eliminate piezoelectric pump noise.

steps.title: Prepare 10× Stock Dissection ACSF
steps.instruction: Dissolve for 1 L: 73.20 g NaCl (125 mM), 1.86 g KCl (2.5 mM), 1.50 g NaH₂PO₄ (1.25 mM), 21.84 g NaHCO₃ (26 mM). Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 10× Stock Recording ACSF
steps.instruction: Dissolve for 1 L: 69.00 g NaCl (118 mM), 2.61 g KCl (3.5 mM), 1.50 g NaH₂PO₄ (1.25 mM), 20.15 g NaHCO₃ (24 mM). Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Make 1× Dissection ACSF (Day of Experiment)
steps.instruction: To 100 ml distilled water add 0.5 ml 1 M CaCl₂ (final 0.5 mM), 10 ml 1 M MgCl₂ (final 10 mM), 1.98 g D‑glucose (11 mM), and 100 ml of the 10× Dissection ACSF stock. Oxygenate with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ for ≥20 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Make 1× Recording ACSF (Day of Experiment)
steps.instruction: To 896.2 ml distilled water add 2.5 ml 1 M CaCl₂ (final 2.5 mM), 1.3 ml 1 M MgSO₄ (final 10 mM), 2.71 g D‑glucose (15 mM), and 100 ml of the 10× Recording ACSF stock. Oxygenate with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ for ≥20 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Chill Dissection ACSF
steps.instruction: Place the room‑temperature 1× Dissection ACSF in a –70 °C freezer for 45 min. If ice crystals form, remove them with a small spoon or sieve. Return the solution to the freezer and continue oxygenating at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Interface Recording Chamber
steps.instruction: Heat the water jacket of the interface chamber so the recording bath reaches 31.5 °C. Pre‑heat 250–500 ml of 1× Recording ACSF in a 32 °C water bath while oxygenating with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Start Bath Perfusion
steps.instruction: Begin perfusing the bath with 1× Recording ACSF at 500 µl/min using the recirculation system (all six mp6 pumps set to maximal flow for suction, inflow pumps off).

steps.title: Anesthetize Animal
steps.instruction: Place the rodent in an anesthesia chamber with an isoflurane vaporizer. Deliver 100 % O₂ for 2 min, then 100 % O₂ + 1.5 % isoflurane for 1 min, then 100 % O₂ + 2.5 % isoflurane for 2 min until deeply anesthetized.

steps.title: Decapitate and Ice‑Cold Transfer
steps.instruction: Decapitate with a small‑animal guillotine. Submerge the head in a metal surgical tray on ice inside an icebox filled with oxygenated ice‑cold 1× Dissection ACSF. Complete brain removal within 10 min.

steps.title: Expose Brain
steps.instruction: Using a single‑edge razor blade, cut the scalp. With pointed surgical scissors, cut along the sagittal suture from foramen magnum to forehead, then cut laterally at the foramen magnum, and across the frontal bone along the coronal suture. Pry open the skull with a rongeur, sever cranial nerves with a spatula, and let the brain fall into a 50 ml beaker of ice‑cold oxygenated 1× Dissection ACSF. Transfer the beaker to a 4 °C cold room.

steps.title: Isolate Hippocampi
steps.instruction: Place a 90 mm Pyrex culture petri dish with moistened filter paper as a dissecting platform. Bisect the brain longitudinally; keep the right hemibrain in a 50 ml beaker of ice‑cold ACSF. For the left hemibrain, remove midbrain and brainstem with a flat spatula, scoop out thalamus, and expose the ventral hippocampal face. Sever septal and temporal hippocampal connections with a spatula. Inject a few droplets of ice‑cold ACSF into the lateral ventricle to outline the fimbria, then insert a fine brush moistened with ACSF and roll the hippocampus out of the cortex. Cut the hippocampus free from cortex, place it in a 20 ml beaker of ice‑cold ACSF. Repeat for the right hippocampus.

steps.title: Prepare Slicing Stage
steps.instruction: Glue a circular cork pad (diameter matching the McIlwain tissue chopper disc) onto a flat surface with parallel strips of double‑sided adhesive tape. Adjust the chopper clamps to match the thickness of this stage. Place a filter paper on the stage and moisten with chilled oxygenated 1× Dissection ACSF.

steps.title: Mount Hippocampus for Slicing
steps.instruction: Lift the isolated hippocampus with a fine brush or bent spatula and lay it dorsal‑side up on the moistened filter paper. Straighten the ventral (bottom) surface so it lies flush. Pin the ventral end to the cork with an insect pin.

steps.title: Set Blade Angle
steps.instruction: Rotate the slicing stage 15° counter‑clockwise for left hippocampus (or 15° clockwise for right) so the dorsal hippocampus is oriented at a 15° angle to the transverse axis of the blade. Wet the blade with ACSF.

steps.title: Slice Hippocampus
steps.instruction: Lower the blade through the tissue, allowing each slice to stick to the wet blade surface as it ascends. Discard the first three most dorsal slices. Collect 6–8 slices of ~450 µm thickness from rats (or 4–5 from mice) by gently rolling a moistened fine sable brush over the blade to lift each slice.

steps.title: Collect Slices in Cold ACSF
steps.instruction: Immediately transfer each slice to a test tube containing ice‑cold oxygenated 1× Dissection ACSF. Avoid stretching or bending; use a brush pre‑moistened with ACSF and a gentle rolling motion.

steps.title: Recover Slices in Interface Chamber
steps.instruction: Place slices onto the mesh of the interface recording chamber, forming a small meniscus around each. Superfuse continuously with non‑recirculating 1× Recording ACSF at 500 µl/min from both top and bottom. Allow at least 2 h recovery before experiments.

steps.title: Program ODN Perfusion (Top Arduino)
steps.instruction: Load the Arduino program from Figure 18 onto the top Arduino (Microcontroller 1). Change the “delay” constant to 1800000 (ms) for a 30‑min perfusion, save, and re‑upload.

steps.title: Program ODN Perfusion (Bottom Arduino)
steps.instruction: Load the Arduino program from Figure 19 onto the bottom Arduino (Microcontroller 2). Change “int32_t clockfrequency” to 200 (gives ~5 ml/min flow), save, and re‑upload.

steps.title: Switch to Recirculation Mode
steps.instruction: Turn off the peristaltic pump and vacuum suction. Activate the piezoelectric pump circuit with the SPST master switch. Use a three‑way valve to select the 15 ml conical tube containing 5 ml of 20 µM ODN in 1× Recording ACSF (drawn from the same water bath as the main reservoir).

steps.title: Start ODN Perfusion
steps.instruction: Run the winLTP program with Sequential Protocol Scripting and Automated Perfusion Control. The ADC digital output will trigger the top Arduino to turn on all six mp6 pumps for 30 min, recirculating 5 ml of ODN‑containing solution at 5 ml/min (Figure 20).

steps.title: Return to Interface Recording
steps.instruction: After 30 min, lower the aspirator tube to bring the bath level back to the interface level. Change the bottom Arduino “int32_t clockfrequency” from 200 to 10, reload the program (Figure 20) to set flow to 0.5 ml/min for the remainder of the experiment.

steps.title: Begin Electrophysiology Recording
steps.instruction: Place a glass extracellular recording electrode (2–5 MΩ) in CA1 stratum radiatum and bipolar stimulating electrodes on either side of CA3 or CA1. Verify slice health (fEPSP spike threshold ≥2 mV). Set baseline fEPSP at 25 % of threshold, stimulate at 0.033 Hz. Induce LTP with two 100 Hz‑1 s tetanic trains spaced 20 s apart (rat: 70 % of threshold; mouse: 25 %). Record field EPSPs and analyze maximum slope using WinLTP.
